paragraphs: My name is Lily, and I am ten years old. We study the months of the year in Teacher Kim's class. Since Monday, we have a birthday list on the board. Teacher Kim wrote the months from January to December. Every child got a white paper picture and glue. We glued our picture in the month of our birthday. "Say your birthday with a number word," said Teacher Kim. "The first, the second, the third." Mia said, "My birthday is on the third of February."

Leo said, "Mine is on the twelfth of May." I said, "Mine is on the twentieth of July." Then Teacher Kim said, "Make a line by birthday." The line started at half past nine. A girl with a January birthday was the first. Mia stood in the third place. Leo stood in the twelfth place, but he was almost asleep. "Leo, wake up!" said Mia. Leo opened his eyes. "You are the twelfth," I said, and he laughed.

I stood in the twenty-first place. After me, a boy with a birthday in September stood in the twenty-second place. A girl with a birthday in December was the last. For December, we glued a snowball. There is no snow in Thailand, but it is winter in cold countries. "A big cake for every child is expensive," said Teacher Kim. "So we sing and clap for each birthday." We all clapped.

At ten o'clock, the list was ready. Our class has a picture in every month. Mia is in February, Leo is in May, and I am in July. "Which month has the most birthdays?" asked Mia. We counted the pictures one by one. It was fun. There were five in October. Number words help us in a line and on a list. Our birthdays are now on the wall for the whole year.
